title: It starts by itself.
kit: Block 3 · the idea
It starts by itself.
Flow
A set of steps in Power Automate that runs on its own when something happens: a trigger, then actions, sometimes a condition.
Copilot and agents wait for you…

title: Before you build one, ask four questions.
kit: Block 3 · what a flow needs
Before you build one, ask four questions.
Ask your IT team first. Then build small.
License: does your Microsoft 365 account include Power Automate?
Permission: does your IT team allow these connectors?
Owner: who fixes it when it breaks, or when someone leaves?
People: is every approval still made by a person?

title: Why not Copilot or an agent?
kit: Block 3 · why a flow here
Why not Copilot or an agent?
A flow moves work between people. It never replaces their decisions.
It starts on its own when a form arrives. Copilot and agents wait to be asked.
It waits for an approval, for days if needed, then continues.
It writes the log and sends the email the same way every time.
It decides nothing. The manager approves; the flow carries the request.

title: Four problems to look for.
kit: Block 4 · four problems
Four problems to look for.
Find them first. Fix them after.
Problem
What it looks like
Ask
Delay
A step waits for days, often for one person.
How long does it wait, and for whom?
Duplicated effort
The same information is typed, printed or checked more than once.
Who types or checks it again?
Unclear ownership
Nobody is sure who does the next step, or who chases it.
Who does the next step? Who chases it?
Repetitive step
The same manual action every time, with no judgment in it.
Is there any judgment in it?
